source.note: Scan without a text layer. National Senior Certificate paper (cover: NATIONAL SENIOR CERTIFICATE; running header: NSC). The PDF includes the cover (printed page 1), the instructions (page 2) and the information sheet (page 15); PDF page n = printed page n. The cover states that the question paper consists of 14 pages, 1 information sheet and an answer book of 24 pages, which is not in this PDF. Duration 3 hours as printed on the cover. Source file and hash are recorded in sources/maths/manifest.json.

extraction.method: manual transcription from 170 dpi page renders, checked at 400 dpi where needed

questions.stem_md: The table below shows the monthly income (in rands) of $6$ different people and the amount (in rands) that each person spends on the monthly repayment of a motor vehicle.

questions.text_md: Determine the equation of the least squares regression line for the data.
If a person earns R$14\,000$ per month, predict the monthly repayment that the person could make towards a motor vehicle.
Determine the correlation coefficient between the monthly income and the monthly repayment of a motor vehicle.

A person who earns R$18\,000$ per month has to decide whether to spend R$9\,000$ as a monthly repayment of a motor vehicle, or not. If the above information is a true representation of the population data, which of the following would the person most likely decide on:

A  Spend R$9\,000$ per month because there is a very strong positive correlation between the amount earned and the monthly repayment.

B  NOT to spend R$9\,000$ per month because there is a very weak positive correlation between the amount earned and the monthly repayment.

C  Spend R$9\,000$ per month because the point $(18\,000\,;\,9\,000)$ lies very near to the least squares regression line.

D  NOT to spend R$9\,000$ per month because the point $(18\,000\,;\,9\,000)$ lies very far from the least squares regression line.

questions.stem_md: A survey was conducted among $100$ people about the amount that they paid on a monthly basis for their cellphone contracts. The person carrying out the survey calculated the estimated mean to be R$309$ per month. Unfortunately, he lost some of the data thereafter. The partial results of the survey are shown in the frequency table below:

questions.text_md: How many people paid R$200$ or less on their monthly cellphone contracts?
Use the information above to show that $a=24$ and $b=16$.
Write down the modal class for the data.
On the grid provided in the ANSWER BOOK, draw an ogive (cumulative frequency graph) to represent the data.
Determine how many people paid more than R$420$ per month for their cellphone contracts.

questions.stem_md: In the diagram, P, $\mathrm{R}(3\,;\,5)$, $\mathrm{S}(-3\,;\,-7)$ and $\mathrm{T}(-5\,;\,k)$ are vertices of trapezium PRST and $\mathrm{PT}\parallel\mathrm{RS}$. RS and PR cut the $y$-axis at D and $\mathrm{C}(0\,;\,5)$ respectively. PT and RS cut the $x$-axis at E and F respectively. $\mathrm{P}\hat{\mathrm{E}}\mathrm{F}=\theta$.

questions.text_md: Write down the equation of PR.
Gradient of RS
Size of $\theta$
Coordinates of D
If it is given that $\mathrm{TS}=2\sqrt{5}$, calculate the value of $k$.
Parallelogram TDNS, with N in the $4^{\text{th}}$ quadrant, is drawn. Calculate the coordinates of N.
$\triangle$PRD is reflected about the $y$-axis to form $\triangle\mathrm{P}'\mathrm{R}'\mathrm{D}'$. Calculate the size of $\mathrm{R}\hat{\mathrm{D}}\mathrm{R}'$.
questions.notes: Reflection of $\triangle$PRD about the $y$-axis, then the angle $\mathrm{R}\hat{\mathrm{D}}\mathrm{R}'$. No dedicated skill for reflection in the $y$-axis (as opposed to $y=x$); tagged with ageo.inclination-angle.

questions.stem_md: In the diagram, a circle having centre M touches the $x$-axis at $\mathrm{A}(-1\,;\,0)$ and the $y$-axis at $\mathrm{B}(0\,;\,1)$. A smaller circle, centred at $\mathrm{N}\left(-\dfrac{1}{2}\,;\,\dfrac{3}{2}\right)$, passes through M and cuts the larger circle at B and C. BNC is a diameter of the smaller circle. A tangent drawn to the smaller circle at C, cuts the $x$-axis at D.

questions.text_md: Determine the equation of the circle centred at M in the form $(x-a)^{2}+(y-b)^{2}=r^{2}$
Calculate the coordinates of C.
Show that the equation of the tangent CD is $y-x=3$.
Determine the values of $t$ for which the line $y=x+t$ will NOT touch or cut the smaller circle.
The smaller circle centred at N is transformed such that point C is translated along the tangent to D. Calculate the coordinates of E, the new centre of the smaller circle.
questions.notes: Translation of the smaller circle along vector $\overrightarrow{\mathrm{CD}}$. No dedicated translation-of-a-circle skill; tagged with fn.translate-graph and ageo.distance-formula.

questions.text_md: If it is given that the area of quadrilateral OBCD is $2a^{2}$ square units and $a>0$, show that $a=\dfrac{\sqrt{7}}{2}$ units.
questions.notes: Area of quadrilateral OBCD from the given coordinates. No dedicated coordinate-area skill; tagged with ageo.distance-formula.

questions.text_md:
Simplify the following expression to ONE trigonometric term:

$\dfrac{\sin x}{\cos x\cdot\tan x}+\sin(180^{\circ}+x)\cos(90^{\circ}-x)$
**Without using a calculator**, determine the value of:  $\dfrac{\sin^{2}35^{\circ}-\cos^{2}35^{\circ}}{4\sin 10^{\circ}\cos 10^{\circ}}$

Given: $\cos 26^{\circ}=m$

**Without using a calculator**, determine $2\sin^{2}77^{\circ}$ in terms of $m$.
Determine the general solution of $f(x)=\tan 165^{\circ}$
Determine the value(s) of $x$ in the interval $x\in[0^{\circ}\,;\,360^{\circ}]$ for which $f(x)$ will have a minimum value.

questions.stem_md: In the diagram, the graphs of $f(x)=\sin x-1$ and $g(x)=\cos 2x$ are drawn for the interval $x\in[-90^{\circ}\,;\,360^{\circ}]$. Graphs $f$ and $g$ intersect at A. $\mathrm{B}(360^{\circ}\,;\,-1)$ is a point on $f$.

questions.text_md: Write down the range of $f$.
Write down the values of $x$ in the interval $x\in[-90^{\circ}\,;\,360^{\circ}]$ for which graph $f$ is decreasing.
P and Q are points on graphs $g$ and $f$ respectively such that PQ is parallel to the $y$-axis. If PQ lies between A and B, determine the value(s) of $x$ for which PQ will be a maximum.

questions.stem_md: The diagram below shows a solar panel, ABCD, which is fixed to a flat piece of concrete slab EFCD. ABCD and EFCD are two identical rhombuses. K is a point on DC such that $\mathrm{DK}=\mathrm{KC}$ and $\mathrm{AK}\perp\mathrm{DC}$. AF and KF are drawn. $\mathrm{A}\hat{\mathrm{D}}\mathrm{C}=\mathrm{C}\hat{\mathrm{D}}\mathrm{E}=60^{\circ}$ and $\mathrm{AD}=x$ units.

questions.text_md: Determine AK in terms of $x$.
Write down the size of $\mathrm{K}\hat{\mathrm{C}}\mathrm{F}$.
It is further given that $\mathrm{A}\hat{\mathrm{K}}\mathrm{F}$, the angle between the solar panel and the concrete slab, is $y$. Determine the area of $\triangle$AKF in terms of $x$ and $y$.

questions.stem_md: In the diagram, PQRS is a cyclic quadrilateral. Chord RS is produced to T. K is a point on RS and W is a point on the circle such that QRKW is a parallelogram. PS and QW intersect at U. $\mathrm{P}\hat{\mathrm{S}}\mathrm{T}=136^{\circ}$ and $\hat{\mathrm{Q}}_{1}=100^{\circ}$.

questions.text_md: Determine, with reasons, the size of: $\hat{\mathrm{R}}$
$\hat{\mathrm{P}}$
$\mathrm{P}\hat{\mathrm{Q}}\mathrm{W}$
$\hat{\mathrm{U}}_{2}$

$\mathrm{EF}=9$ units, $\mathrm{DC}=18$ units, $\mathrm{ET}=7$ units, $\mathrm{TC}=10$ units, $\mathrm{FT}=5$ units and $\mathrm{TD}=14$ units.

$\mathrm{D}\hat{\mathrm{F}}\mathrm{C}=\mathrm{D}\hat{\mathrm{E}}\mathrm{C}$

questions.stem_md: In the diagram, O is the centre of the circle. ST is a tangent to the circle at T. M and P are points on the circle such that $\mathrm{TM}=\mathrm{MP}$. OT, OP and TP are drawn. Let $\hat{\mathrm{O}}_{1}=x$.
questions.text_md: Prove, with reasons, that $\mathrm{S}\hat{\mathrm{T}}\mathrm{M}=\dfrac{1}{4}x$.

questions.stem_md: In the diagram, $\triangle$ABC is drawn. D is a point on AB and E is a point on AC such that $\mathrm{DE}\parallel\mathrm{BC}$. BE and DC are drawn.
questions.text_md: Use the diagram to prove the theorem which states that a line drawn parallel to one side of a triangle divides the other two sides proportionally, in other words prove that $\dfrac{\mathrm{AD}}{\mathrm{DB}}=\dfrac{\mathrm{AE}}{\mathrm{EC}}$

(a) WSTV is a cyclic quadrilateral
(b) $\triangle$WRV is isosceles
(c) $\triangle$WRV $|||$ $\triangle$TSV
(d) $\dfrac{\mathrm{RV}}{\mathrm{SR}}=\dfrac{\mathrm{KV}}{\mathrm{TS}}$
